turns.doctor_question: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?
turns.patient_response:
Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for fitting me in. It’s lovely to meet you, too. 

I, um... well, I hope I'm not making a fuss over nothing. I'm a secondary school teacher, and lately I've just been having a bit of a hard time shaking off some... thoughts, I guess? 

It sounds a bit silly when I say it out loud, and I know it probably sounds strange, but I keep getting this feeling that certain staff emails, or even the morning announcements over the PA system, are actually... well, coded messages meant specifically for me. 

Some of the other teachers—who are just wonderful, by the way—they've gently shown me that those emails are just standard memos sent to everyone on staff. And I know they are! I really do. But I just can't quite seem to shake the feeling that they're about me anyway. 

Is that... is that the sort of thing I should be bringing up today? I just want to make sure I'm explaining things the right way for you.

turns.doctor_question: Have you heard voices when no one else was there?
turns.patient_response:
Oh... um... well. I suppose... and I really hope this doesn't make me sound completely unhinged, doctor... but, yes. Sometimes. 

It's only ever when it's very quiet. Like when I'm at home by myself, or after all the students have left my classroom for the day and I'm just tidying up. I'll hear... well, a woman's voice. Usually she's just saying my name, or maybe making a very short little comment about whatever I happen to be doing at that moment. 

It's so brief, really! But it sounds clear enough that a few times I've actually answered back out loud, just out of habit, before I look up and realize the room is completely empty. 

I always tell myself it's just stress, or my ears playing tricks on me when I'm tired. I really hope that doesn't sound too alarming... I just want to be completely honest with you so you have the right picture. Is... is that the kind of thing you needed to know?
